status.label: Reproduce fallback identity/persistence
status.detail: The latest report supplies repeated fallback IDs, so the earlier fixed/owned classification is not justified.

next_action.label: Reproduce duplicate fallback identifiers
next_action.reason: Determine whether ordering is lost in identity mapping, persistence, or provider reload.

judgment.rationale: The report supplies a reorder/OK/reopen sequence, recording, diagnostic ZIP and later duplicate-ID settings excerpt. A September build appeared fixed to one commenter, but the October 12 report supplies contrary evidence.
evidence: The original reproduction is on 0.99.1; the reporter still saw the issue on 0.100.2.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/47829#issuecomment-6121597515 shows repeated com.microsoft.powertoys.fallback identifiers and partially saved changes.
Inspected SettingsViewModel.cs rebuilds rankings with currentRankings.IndexOf(fallback.Id) and persists FallbackRankings.Select(...Id).
Merged PR 50799 addresses initial global fallback defaults, not unique ordering of duplicate fallback identities; it is not proof this report is fixed.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the existing public sequence with duplicate fallback IDs, then review the identity/persistence plan before implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No verified targeted implementation covers the latest duplicate-ID/order-reset report; an identity round-trip correction is a supported hypothesis.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve distinct fallback identities across rank persistence
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: fallback entries that share an Id cannot retain independent ranks because reconstruction uses the first IndexOf match and persistence saves only Id strings. A provider reload/save race remains an alternative.
plan: Reproduce reorder/OK/reopen with multiple entries sharing the public reported fallback ID, recording the ordered command identities before and after ApplyFallbackSort.

Trace fallback identity production into SettingsViewModel and SettingsModel; define a stable provider-and-command identity when the contract permits duplicates, or fix the producer if IDs must be unique.
Migrate existing FallbackRanks deterministically without discarding user order; do not merely Distinct the list and silently merge different commands.
Add ranking round-trip tests for duplicate IDs, provider load order, missing providers, and reopening settings; preserve intentionally disabled/global-result choices.
verification: Reorder, accept, close and reopen settings, then restart Command Palette; distinct commands retain their order.
Test both unique-ID built-in providers and a synthetic provider exposing repeated IDs.
Confirm new provider defaults do not overwrite existing user ranks.

confidence.rationale: The latest serialized duplicate IDs and first-match reconstruction align directly; no runtime trace yet proves whether identity ambiguity or a competing save is decisive.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette fallback order reverts after accepting settings. Later evidence of repeated fallback IDs contradicts an earlier claim that new builds fixed it.
known_information: The report already includes a recording, screenshot and diagnostic archive.
The reporter confirmed continued failure on 0.100.2.
The latest commenter supplies repeated fallback identifiers and says only some changes persist.
There is no assignee or direct linked fix on the issue timeline.
inferences: Persisting ranks by a non-unique identifier may make the user's order ambiguous; persistence races are not ruled out.
issue_context.analysis: The public evidence is sufficient for a focused maintainer reproduction. Asking for another generic diagnostic ZIP would not distinguish the identity and save paths as efficiently as tracing the supplied case.
initial_investigation: Read the body and all five comments and inspected the full timeline.
Inspected SettingsViewModel fallback-rank reconstruction and ApplyFallbackSort.
Checked related merged fallback-default work and found no demonstrated coverage for duplicate-ID ordering.

actions.label: Review fallback identity fix plan
actions.description: Approve the bounded investigation/fix plan; this lightweight proposal is not a converged implementation-grade design.

prerequisites: Use the latest stable build, recording its version, and a development build for tracing.
Use multiple fallback commands, including a synthetic provider with repeated IDs; back up settings.
steps: Open fallback order settings and record command names and IDs.
Reorder several commands, select OK, close settings and reopen.
Repeat after restarting Command Palette; compare FallbackRanks with displayed order.
Trace IDs and settings writes at ApplyFallbackSort and provider enumeration to distinguish ambiguous IDs from overwrite timing.
reproduce.expected_result: The accepted order survives reopen/restart and each distinct fallback remains distinguishable.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare an isolated Command Palette development provider with two distinct named fallback commands sharing the ID com.microsoft.powertoys.fallback. Keep user settings backed up, then capture the order-to-ID mapping before and after reorder/OK/reopen.
